ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Zora Neale Hurston

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Ms. Hurston returns for her subsequent annual wellness visit; her first was at the county health department clinic before she established care here. She completed the health risk assessment with the medical assistant. Since her eight-week review her blood pressure has stayed at goal at home (average 124/74), she walks to the bus and back without stopping, and her ankles no longer swell. The lightheadedness in the May heat has not come back since she changed her gardening hours. Her drug plan with Extra Help began in the summer, and her medicines now cost a few dollars a month. School has started again and she is being called to substitute. She has no new concerns but asks what screening she is due for, since she has not had a mammogram or a colon test in many years. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She has not written down her wishes before. She named a close friend from her hometown as her health care surrogate, and the Florida designation form was completed and copied into the chart. She wants full treatment for illness she can recover from. If a stroke or other illness left her unable to read, write or recognize the people she knows, with little chance of recovery, she would not want resuscitation or long-term life support, and would want to be kept comfortable at home if possible. She will tell her surrogate. She asked that her papers and manuscripts go to a university library rather than be thrown away. [S]
